opportunities.title: Run a complete sale on merchant-owned Bitcoin and other tenders
opportunities.merchant_job: Sell an itemized basket, take Bitcoin/cash/optional card, issue a correct receipt, handle exceptions, and reconcile a shift; later support additional retail, restaurant, and online workflows when validated.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: Adds a payment method whose on-chain receipt can be verified independently of the card processor; merchant can retain the sale ledger and key authority locally.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: Bitcoin does not supply a basket, tax/modifier engine, inventory, staff workflow, physical receipts, or day-close accounting. The first measured retail workflow is proposed validation sequencing; restaurant and online needs remain backlog rather than rejected product jobs.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Local canonical sale journal with immutable basket and independent tender attempts; integrate on-chain and cash first, with optional replaceable card adapter and separately gated Shop Lightning receiving. Extend the same sale contract to validated restaurant and online workflows.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Local-first operation reduces backend dependence but makes durable storage, backup, reconciliation and recovery the product’s responsibility. A completed retail validation scenario does not establish restaurant or online coverage.
opportunities.validation_needed: Complete observed retail shifts on named devices; measure setup, checkout time, partial/late/excess recovery, receipt correctness, inventory/refund accuracy, day close, and support burden.

opportunities.title: Accept on-chain Bitcoin under merchant key authority
opportunities.merchant_job: Receive payment directly to merchant-controlled keys, recover independently, and keep checkout staff from gaining spend authority.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: Supports direct receiving to merchant-controlled keys and independent recovery without required company permission over funds; checkout staff can use public-only watch access while owner-approved bounded spend automation remains a design candidate.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: Self-custody does not remove key loss, device security, backup testing, privacy leakage, or staff training risks; a seed alone does not restore the merchant application ledger. Owner-approved automated spending requires explicit authority bounds and architecture proof.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Merchant hot wallet or independently created cold wallet, public-only pairing, independently verified receive address, durable issued-address mapping and merchant-held recovery artifacts. Evaluate bounded, owner-authorized signing/UTXO protection without changing signing behavior before proof and review.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Authority and possible provider independence come with direct responsibility for key protection, backups, safe address derivation, and incident recovery.
opportunities.validation_needed: Clean-device restore, watch-only pairing without secret exposure, register role denial of spend/authority changes, and correct address verification on the signer’s own display.

opportunities.title: Make payment state and sale exceptions honest
opportunities.merchant_job: Know whether a request is unpaid, partial, overpaid, late, unconfirmed, confirmed, conflicted, reorganized, expired, refunded, or unresolved before fulfillment.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: On-chain transaction and confirmation evidence can be independently checked and tied to a specific request; the merchant need not treat processor messages as the source of Bitcoin truth.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: A transaction can be late, replaceable, unconfirmed, reorganized, partial, or sent after cancellation. One confirmation is not a universal fulfillment policy and an address does not expire on-chain.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Durable request-to-sale mapping and observation journal with freshness/depth, immutable transaction references, explicit exception states, idempotent reconciliation, and separate fulfillment permission.
opportunities.tradeoffs: More accurate distinctions add cashier exception work and may delay fulfillment; simplistic instant-paid indicators increase loss or duplicate-fulfillment risk.
opportunities.validation_needed: Regtest unseen/unconfirmed/confirmed/conflicting/reorged, partial/excess/duplicate, expired/late, crash/restart and restored-ledger cases; merchant selects confirmation and fulfillment policy.

opportunities.title: Control receiving and spending cost decisions
opportunities.merchant_job: Understand incoming-output future spend economics and approve outbound fee, destination, and input use with protection against avoidable UTXO loss.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: Direct merchant control can make fee timing, UTXO selection and spend authorization visible rather than hiding them inside a processor payout schedule.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: Bitcoin cannot guarantee low fees or rapid confirmation. Tiny outputs can cost more to spend than their value; fee ceilings may delay transactions. Any automated spend behavior must be bounded and owner-approved; fresh addresses do not establish recipient identity.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Read-only satoshi/UTXO cost advisory plus a research candidate for bounded UTXO protection and fee-aware owner-approved signing, with explicit transaction preview, durable input reservation and limits. Preserve current signing behavior until architecture proof and review pass.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Advisory-only status is the current code boundary, not a permanent product limit. Automation can protect against uneconomic outputs but adds authority, race, recovery and fee-estimation risks; unbounded spending would violate the intended authority model.
opportunities.validation_needed: Define amount/fee/UTXO bounds, failure behavior, rollback and owner controls; test fee changes, dust-sized receipts, reservation races, invalid/wrong-network refund destinations, actual fee versus approved bounds, recovery and signer display. No hard maximum-loss guarantee.

opportunities.title: Offer Lightning as a separately gated receiving mode
opportunities.merchant_job: Offer Shop Lightning as a core Bitcoin receiving goal when the merchant-controlled node is funded, operational, backed up and has usable inbound liquidity.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: Can support rapid wallet-to-wallet receiving without on-chain confirmation for each retail sale and can be operated under merchant node authority.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: It does not provide guaranteed routes, free or prepaid inbound capacity, zero downtime, instant exit, or channel-state independence from current persistent state and counterparties.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Merchant-operated Shop Lightning receiving as a core goal, with honest opt-in/setup and readiness gates for confirmed funding, usable inbound capacity, node availability, backup freshness, MPP support and independent exit. Select on-chain-first launch ordering only as a proposed release sequence; persist ChannelManager/Monitor state safely and document close/sweep path.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Faster checkout requires channel capital, inbound liquidity, connectivity, careful backups and recovery operations; force-close can incur on-chain fees and time locks. A separate initial on-chain-first release is a proposed sequencing choice, not an exclusion of Shop Lightning.
opportunities.validation_needed: Named LDK/node version and wallets; funding confirmation, directionality, liquidity acquisition cost, routing fees/failures, MPP, outage, stale backup, peer loss, reorg and unilateral exit trials.

opportunities.title: Keep payment privacy and checkout service local by default
opportunities.merchant_job: Take payment and retain sale history without mandatory company-server approval, sales-history upload, customer identity collection, or exposure of needless metadata.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: A direct wallet payment can avoid sending full payment credentials and sale records to a payment processor; merchant can use one-time addresses and local mapping.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: Public blockchain activity remains observable and can be linked; address rotation is not anonymity. Local-only operation does not itself solve secure backup, device compromise, or optional service disclosure.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Local journal, minimal opaque payment-request references, fresh addresses, privacy-reviewed exports, opt-in scoped webhooks only, and no required publisher ledger or telemetry.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Reducing central data collection can limit remote support, consolidated analytics and automatic multi-site views; opting into integrations creates additional disclosed data paths.
opportunities.validation_needed: Inspect URI/QR/NFC payloads, receipts, logs, exports, webhook payload/signature/retry behavior, retention and permission boundaries; test operation with no company endpoint.

opportunities.title: Continue cashier work through outages without inventing settlement
opportunities.merchant_job: Keep a sale and permitted cash/card workflows usable when network, processor, or Lightning is unavailable, then reconcile uncertain tenders safely.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: Cash/on-chain choices may remain available independently of a card provider, and merchant-operated infrastructure can avoid a mandatory company server for local checkout.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: Bitcoin cannot be settled by a disconnected cashier or node; an offline QR/address display is only a request, not proof of received payment. Card offline authorization is provider-specific and may carry delayed decline risk.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Local sale journal and cash fallback; mark card response unknown until reconciliation; disable Lightning when node status is stale; show on-chain request only as unpaid until a trusted observer catches up.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Availability differs by tender; safe status can be less convenient than an optimistic paid marker and reconciliation may require staff attention after reconnect.
opportunities.validation_needed: App kill, power/network loss, card timeout, node disconnection, remote sync conflicts, repeated attempts and post-outage reconciliation on target devices without duplicate charge or fulfillment.

opportunities.title: Reconcile refunds, receipts and day close across tender rails
opportunities.merchant_job: Tell the customer what was sold, what was received, what is owed/refunded, and reconcile exact tender totals at shift close.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: On-chain receipts and transactions provide independently reconcilable satoshi amounts and timestamps; direct merchant refunds can avoid asking an original processor to authorize Bitcoin funds.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: A Bitcoin refund is a new spend with fee, destination, confirmation and authorization risks; a receipt or invoice does not prove settlement. Bitcoin does not determine tax treatment, card refund eligibility, inventory or accounting.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Canonical sale/tender/refund ledger; record refund requested/owed/paid separately, require a fresh destination and owner approval for on-chain payout, and export exact amounts with privacy disclosure.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Explicit tender-level reconciliation is more accurate but entails staff handling for exceptions and careful non-duplicative refund processing.
opportunities.validation_needed: Multi-tender partial refunds, canceled/late/excess payment, crash/retry, destination replacement, actual transaction match, receipts and day-close totals across Bitcoin/cash/card.

opportunities.title: Keep card processing optional and replaceable
opportunities.merchant_job: Accept cards when a merchant-approved provider/device is available without making that provider authoritative for Bitcoin keys or sale truth.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: Merchant-controlled Bitcoin acceptance can remain available if card integration or account access changes, and card access can be isolated from Bitcoin signing authority.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: Bitcoin does not grant card-network acceptance, production eligibility, reader support, country/account eligibility, chargeback handling, or card offline approval.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Tender adapter boundary with durable card attempt IDs and unknown-response reconciliation; provider tokens and processor permissions isolated from Bitcoin wallet authority; cash/on-chain remain standalone.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Provider independence requires maintaining adapter behavior and target-device certification; additional adapters increase operations and support scope.
opportunities.validation_needed: Supported production account/country/device/physical reader evidence, lost response/duplicate/cancel/refund recovery, provider outage independence, privacy review and key isolation.

opportunities.title: Support recurring merchant billing without assuming universal wallet auto-debit
opportunities.merchant_job: Set up recurring subscriptions, present each cycle’s amount and due status, and follow up on missing payments.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_improves: A merchant can issue a new on-chain or Lightning request for each billing cycle and reconcile direct settlement per cycle.
opportunities.what_bitcoin_does_not_improve: A payment request is not standing authority to debit a customer’s self-custody wallet. The protocol does not guarantee arbitrary recurring pull payments, customer approval, funds availability, or successful delivery.
opportunities.architecture_candidate: Recurring schedule emits a distinct amount/network-scoped payment request per cycle with lifecycle notices and cancellation; customer initiates each payment. Treat any separately authorized spending arrangement as a distinct mechanism requiring explicit scope and revocation.
opportunities.tradeoffs: Customer-initiated invoices preserve explicit per-cycle wallet control but may add renewal friction and missed-payment follow-up; standing authorization could reduce friction while adding authority, revocation and dispute risks.
opportunities.validation_needed: Test recurring invoice generation, amount changes, cancel/pause/resume, late/partial/duplicate payments, failed notices, invoice expiry, reconciliation, and customer cancellation; separately review any proposed reusable spending authority.
